answer: In a robotic marine haven, Sybil attacks are curtailed through optical phase anchoring. Agents verify distinct locations by sampling carrier phase shifts from a fixed navigation lantern pulsing in the violet spectrum. Creating fake identities forces an adversary to deploy separate, physical sensor masts across the water, incurring substantial hardware expenses. However, thick sea spray and atmospheric scattering degrade signal coherence, occasionally misclassifying genuine agents.
